sections.h2: Selling a house in Wyoming, Michigan
sections.html:
Wyoming, with about 78,600 residents, is a Kent County city on the southwest side of the Grand Rapids area, and only Grand Rapids itself is larger in West Michigan. Selling a house here involves the city Assessor's Office for transfer paperwork, the Kent County Register of Deeds in downtown Grand Rapids for recording, and a few city codes that surface during a buyer's inspection.

This page covers Wyoming, Michigan, which has no tie to the state of Wyoming. The sections run in the order of a sale: the local market, the city's rules, and the filings that follow closing.

Wyoming became a city in 1959 and grew up around manufacturing. The 28th Street strip is the regional shopping corridor, with new retail also toward RiverTown Crossings. The city has 21 parks on about 665 acres and ties into the Kent Trails bike network.

Manufacturing is the largest local industry, and the biggest employers are:

  • Gordon Food Service, 5,000 workers.
  • Metro Health Hospital, 3,000.
  • GM Components Holdings, 1,200.
  • ABC Technologies, 650, and Benteler, 580.

US-131 cuts north and south through the middle of the city, M-11 (28th Street) crosses it east to west, and M-6 touches the southern edge. Eight of The Rapid's routes serve Wyoming. Workers here report a mean commute of 21.9 minutes.

Eight school districts overlap the city: Wyoming Public Schools in the center, Godwin Heights in the northeast, Godfrey-Lee in the north, Kelloggsville in the southeast, Kentwood below 56th Street and east of the tracks, Grandville in the southwest, Byron Center near Metro Health, and a sliver of Grand Rapids Public Schools. Verify the district by street address.

The 2025 estimate of 78,588 residents is 2.7 percent higher than the 2020 base, up from 72,125 in 2010. Across 2020 through 2024, Wyoming had 29,417 households of about 2.61 people, and 67.1 percent of them were owners.

Homes occupied by their owners have a median value of $225,200. Gross rent has a median of $1,196 and household income $73,677. A typical owner with a mortgage spends $1,398 a month. Rising population and steady local employers mean buyers are active, so a clean certificate and complete paperwork help you close on schedule.

sections.h2: City rules a Wyoming seller should check
sections.html:
Every rental in Wyoming has to be registered and certified, and the BS&A Online portal shows the status for any address. If you are selling a rented house, check that the certificate is current before a buyer finds an open violation. A short-term rental of 27 days or less must also register, at no cost and without an inspection.

Inspections, at 1155 28th St. SW (616-530-7285), issues building, electrical, mechanical and plumbing permits. Homeowners can apply online with no account, and most residential permits take one to two weeks. A buyer's inspector may flag these maintenance items:

  • Lawn grass or weeds over 10 inches.
  • Trash containers visible from the front of the house.
  • Cars on unpaved ground, or unlicensed vehicles outside a garage.
  • Fences in the required front yard taller than 36 inches.

Backyard hens are allowed by permit. The permit is free, caps a household at four chickens, bans roosters and free-range birds, and starts with a two-week comment period for adjacent neighbors, so a buyer who plans to keep hens should ask whether a permit exists for the house. Owners who want to split or combine a lot file a land division application with the Assessor's Office by the first Monday in October for it to take effect in the next tax year.

sections.h2: Filing with the Wyoming Assessor after a sale
sections.html:
The assessor tracks roughly 25,000 parcels and values them at 50 percent of the usual selling price. Taxable value is capped: it cannot grow each year by more than inflation or 5 percent, whichever is smaller. After a sale, the cap lifts in the following year and taxable value rises to match assessed value.

Each change of ownership goes on a Property Transfer Affidavit, due within 45 days. The title company typically hands over the form at closing. Leaving it out can trigger back taxes, penalties and interest running from the transfer date.

sections.h2: Recording a Wyoming deed in Kent County
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds for Kent County works from 300 Monroe Avenue NW in downtown Grand Rapids and takes cash, checks or money orders made out to the Register of Deeds. The charges are:

  • $30 for a deed, mortgage or other instrument.
  • $5 per deed for treasurer's tax certification of warranty deeds and land contracts, covering up to 25 parcels.
  • $1.10 per thousand of consideration for the county transfer tax.
  • $7.50 per thousand of consideration for the state transfer tax.

The seller or grantor owes the tax, and mortgages owe none. The deed states the full consideration, or a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit is filed at no charge. The office will not supply blank deeds or advise on drafting, so work with a title company or attorney.

If you disagree with your assessed value, start with the March Board of Review. A missed March hearing is not the end: the Michigan Tax Tribunal takes residential appeals until July 31. The July and December boards only correct clerical errors and mutual mistakes and consider certain exemptions.

For a seller, this matters mostly for the buyer's first bill, since taxable value rises to assessed value the year after the sale. Hand the buyer your latest assessment notice so they know what to expect.

sections.h2: Putting a Wyoming sale in order
sections.html: Check the rental certificate if tenants live in the house, and walk the yard against the maintenance list above. Gather permit records for any past work, then call the Inspections office with questions. Collect offers in writing, and for each one note the closing date and who covers transfer tax and title costs. Once you accept, the title company prepares the deed, adds the treasurer certification for a warranty deed, hands over the Property Transfer Affidavit form and records the deed in Grand Rapids. A cash buyer needs no lender appraisal, which removes one common delay.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for a Property Transfer Affidavit after a Wyoming sale?
faqs.a: It is due within 45 days of the transfer. The title company normally supplies the form at closing, and a missed filing can bring back taxes with penalties and interest.

faqs.q: Will the property tax bill on a Wyoming house change after a sale?
faqs.a: For the new owner, yes. The cap on taxable value resets to assessed value the year following a sale, and Wyoming assesses at 50 percent of the usual selling price.

faqs.q: Does a rented Wyoming house need a certificate before it sells?
faqs.a: The city requires every rental to be registered and certified, so a landlord should make sure the certificate is current. The Inspections Department, 616-530-7285, can check the status.

faqs.q: Which office records a Wyoming deed?
faqs.a: The Kent County Register of Deeds, 300 Monroe Avenue NW, Grand Rapids. It charges $30 per document, and a warranty deed also needs the $5 treasurer certification.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal a Wyoming assessment after the March Board of Review?
faqs.a: Yes, through the Michigan Tax Tribunal, which must receive residential appeals by July 31. The July and December boards only correct clerical errors and mutual mistakes and consider certain exemptions.
